claims.text: As-built selectively laser melted CoCrFeNiMn components have comparatively coarse grains.
As-built selectively laser melted CoCrFeNiMn components contain process-induced defects.
Optimized laser surface melting will remelt only the top 50–100 μm of the component.
Laser surface melting will generate a nano-twinned surface microstructure.
Laser surface melting will generate an ultrafine-grained surface microstructure.
The treated surface layer will have fewer metallurgical defects than the untreated surface.
The rapid thermal cycle produced by laser surface melting causes rapid solidification.
Rapid solidification promotes nano-twin formation in laser-surface-melted CoCrFeNiMn.
Rapid solidification refines the grains in the treated surface layer.
Nano-twin formation and grain refinement enhance surface mechanical strength.
Nano-twin formation and grain refinement enhance fatigue resistance.
Optimized laser surface melting will improve wear resistance relative to untreated as-built components.
Optimized laser surface melting will increase high-cycle fatigue life by approximately 10–15% relative to untreated as-built components.
Minimizing process-induced defects is necessary for the predicted fatigue and wear improvements.
The beneficial effects will persist under thermal and mechanical loads typical of aggressive operational environments if surface-melting process control is uniform.
Excessive residual stresses or microcracking produced during treatment can compromise mechanical performance.
The exact laser parameters needed to balance rapid solidification, residual stress, and localized defect formation are uncertain.
